messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: decode-stream svc reporting GPU OOMs and container restarts in us-west-2 cluster. Symptoms: streaming request drops and 5xxs since 09:02 UTC. Paging on-call. thread_ts=2489991111

maria_g: I'm on it — seeing a spike in decode pod restarts, nodes flapping between Ready/NotReady. Adding logs to thread.

jason_h: logs from pod decode-psi-7: `CUDA out of memory: tried to allocate 820MB` repeated, then kubelet restarted container. Stack shows decode loop during streaming.

kevin_s: Confirmed. Also seeing large avg token lengths for certain requests in the last 5m, some > 120k tokens — looks like a runaway generation case.

alex_t: Any recent deploys? deploy-bot: deploy v2.14.3 to decode-stream completed 08:55 UTC — config change included "client_max_tokens" passthrough to runtime.

maria_g: That passthrough change matches the timeline. Looks like clients can now specify arbitrarily large max_tokens and we were trusting it. We usually enforce a default cap, but that validation path appears bypassed in the new code path for streaming.

jason_h: Repro: craft a streaming request with `max_tokens: 100000` -> pod memory climbs and OOM within ~30s. Staging repro attached.

kevin_s: Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback v2.14.3 (blocks passthrough), 2) patch runtime to enforce server-side cap, 3) route traffic to CPU decode nodes (slower but stable), 4) apply cluster-level admission control limiting containers' memory — but restarts will continue. Prefer 1+2+3 in parallel.

maria_g: I'm initiating a rollback now. @deploy-bot start rollback v2.14.2 on decode-stream.

deploy-bot: rollback started -> version v2.14.2 resumed on decode-stream (09:12 UTC).

alex_t: Rolling back reduces new requests, but there are still running sessions with bad max_tokens values in the system that will keep causing OOMs until they finish. Need a short-term reject policy.

jason_h: Patch idea: apply a reverse-proxy header rewrite at ingress to cap `x-client-max-tokens` to 2048. Can push via nginx config change in us-west-2 quickly.

kevin_s: I'm pushing the ingress patch now: `proxy_set_header x-client-max-tokens 2048;` — will apply to streaming route only.

maria_g: Ingress patch applied (09:18 UTC). New requests should be capped, monitoring for OOM events.

jason_h: Also killing a few runaway sessions manually: kubectl exec into problematic pod, list streams and terminate long-lived streams. Command: 
```
kubectl -n inference exec -it <pod> -- /bin/bash
ps aux | grep decode_stream
kill -9 <pid>
```

kevin_s: Running `kubectl get events --field-selector reason=OOMKilled -n inference` — OOMKilled events dropped to near zero after ingress patch and rollback.

cs-rep: Customer impact: Support queue shows 8 customers reported partial transcript drops and 3 reported full request failures between 09:02-09:20 UTC. I have case IDs CS-8421, CS-8422, CS-8423. We should prepare a short post-incident note.

maria_g: Agreed. For now: mitigation summary -> rollback v2.14.2, ingress header cap 2048, manual termination of runaway sessions, and follow-up server-side guard in runtime to enforce a hard max_tokens ceiling.

oncall-sre: I'm taking on-call handoff at 09:23 UTC. Status: system stabilized, OOMs largely mitigated, customer-facing errors minimized but some customers saw degraded streaming. I'll continue monitoring for 60m.

jason_h: Next actions (owners): 1) runtime team (alex_t) add server-side max_tokens hard cap and reject request with 4xx if exceeded (PR by EOD). 2) product/deploy (maria_g) revert client passthrough change from config permanently or gate behind opt-in. 3) ops (kevin_s) add admission policy to prevent pods from exceeding expected memory for decode. 4) cs (cs-rep) prepare customer comms.

alex_t: On it — I'll open RFC + PR to enforce caps at admission point and runtime. Temporary hotfix: runtime will sanitize client field and clamp to 2048 in v2.14.4 if rollback causes gaps.

maria_g: Filing an incident summary for ops and postmortem. Key timeline: 08:55 deploy, 09:02 first OOM alerts, 09:12 rollback started, 09:18 ingress cap applied, 09:23 stabilized & handoff.

cs-rep: I'll draft a brief external note: acknowledge the partial outages, explain caused by a config change allowing client-controlled max_tokens leading to GPU OOMs, list mitigations and next steps.

oncall-sre: Leaving monitoring hooks: alert if OOMKilled events >3 in 5m or error rate >1% on streaming decode route. I've also created a Grafana dashboard bookmark and added throttling SLO.

maria_g: Thanks all — handoff complete. I'll own the postmortem and remediation timeline. Tagging @product-team for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

jason_h: Example logs attached (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T09:04:11Z] decode_stream.cpp:245 allocate_kv_cache(819200000) -> CUDA OOM
[2026-03-15T09:04:12Z] runtime: session 0x7ffdeadbeef length=127893 -> OOMKilled
```

kevin_s: Notes for postmortem: root cause = lack of server-side validation for client-supplied token cap after config change; contributing = rollout without invariant tests, no canary limit for streaming flows. Action items captured in follow-up ticket INF-1128.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=high -> mitigated, owners assigned, follow-up ticket INF-1128.

maria_g: Adding final note for next on-call: if you see residual OOMs, first check `x-client-max-tokens` header counts on requests, then verify ingress cap and active rollbacks. Handoff complete.

oncall-sre: Acknowledged. Monitoring continues for 60m; will escalate if regressions occur.
